title: Principal Full Stack Engineer
description:
**Principal Full Stack Engineer**
---------------------------------

**We are Lennar**


Lennar is one of the nation's leading homebuilders, dedicated to making an impact and creating an extraordinary experience for their Homeowners, Communities, and Associates by building quality homes and providing exceptional customer service, giving back to the communities in which we work and live in, and fostering a culture of opportunity and growth for our Associates throughout their career. Lennar has been recognized as a Fortune 500® company and consistently ranked among the top homebuilders in the United States.


**Join a Company that Empowers you to Build your Future**

We are looking for a Principal Engineer who will fundamentally change how our engineering teams work. Transforming the internal culture, workflows, and platform of our engineering organization to be AI\\-native.


You will be the person who embeds with teams, rolls up your sleeves, and shows engineers firsthand how tools like Claude Code, ChatGPT Codex, and GitHub Copilot paired with agentic CI/CD patterns can compress days of work into hours. You will simultaneously build the platform scaffolding that makes this transformation repeatable, safe, and scalable across the organization. This is a builder and coach role in equal measure and the ideal candidate thrives in both.


* A career with purpose.
* A career built on making dreams come true.
* A career built on building zero defect homes, cost management, and adherence to schedules.

**Your Responsibilities on the Team**

* Embed directly with engineering teams to drive hands\\-on adoption of AI coding tools \\- Claude Code, ChatGPT Codex, GitHub Copilot going beyond demos to changing actual daily habits: AI\\-assisted code review, context\\-aware test generation, and agent\\-driven refactoring workflows.
* Design and run structured transformation programs: onboarding sprints, office hours, lunch\\-and\\-learns, and pairing sessions that meet engineers where they are.
* Build and maintain the internal AI transformation playbook \\- documenting CLAUDE.md conventions, MCP server configurations, agent tool definitions, prompt libraries, and workflow templates that teams can self\\-serve and adapt.
* Partner with engineering managers and tech leads to identify the highest\\-leverage transformation opportunities within each team's existing workflows.
* Redesign CI/CD pipelines to incorporate agentic steps: automated code review agents, AI\\-driven test generation, PR summarization, release note automation, and self\\-healing build workflows.
* Build the internal platform layer that makes AI tooling safe and repeatable at scale \\- guardrails, cost controls, audit logging, prompt governance, and approval workflows for agentic actions.
* Define and implement agentic patterns for platform engineering: IaC agents that auto\\-remediate drift, incident response agents triggered by Coralogix/Grafana alerts, Claude Code sub\\-agents for deployment validation, and multi\\-step orchestration across GitHub Actions and internal tooling.
* Architect integrations between AI tooling and the existing engineering ecosystem: GitHub, Jira, Slack, internal developer portal, observability platforms, and secrets/identity systems \\- ensuring agents operate within defined permission boundaries.
* Own the technical strategy for AI tooling adoption \\- model selection across frontier providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, open\\-source), build vs. buy decisions for agentic infrastructure, token cost management, context window optimization, and responsible deployment practices across the engineering org.
* Establish evaluation frameworks for agentic workflows: LLM\\-as\\-judge harnesses, task completion rate benchmarks, hallucination and tool\\-misuse detection, latency/cost tradeoff analysis, and DORA metric correlation to AI adoption milestones.
* Mentor and elevate senior engineers by modeling AI\\-native engineering practices \\- through design reviews, documentation, pairing, and shared tooling.
* Contribute to cross\\-functional AI governance conversations, ensuring our agentic platform practices align with security, compliance, and organizational risk tolerance.

  

**Requirements**

* 8\\+ years of engineering experience with strong foundations in backend services, APIs, cloud\\-native infrastructure, and containerized deployments.
* Deep CI/CD expertise \\- GitHub Actions, ArgoCD with hands\\-on experience redesigning pipelines to incorporate AI\\-driven steps, agent checkpoints, and human\\-in\\-the\\-loop approval gates.
* Experience in platform engineering, internal developer platforms (IDPs) \\- you understand that engineers are your customers.
* Fluent in GoLang and TypeScript/JavaScript; comfortable writing the glue code, automation scripts, and workflow tooling that makes platforms hum.
* Direct, hands\\-on experience with AI coding tools in production engineering contexts \\- Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or equivalent \\- not just personal use, but driving adoption with others.
* Practical knowledge of LLM integration patterns: structured prompt engineering, tool/function calling, MCP server design, agentic frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex, or custom), context management strategies, and multi\\-step reasoning workflows with defined failure modes.
* Deep understanding of agentic system design \\- how to architect multi\\-step agent workflows with tool use, memory, sandboxed execution environments, human\\-in\\-the\\-loop checkpoints, rollback mechanisms, and token budget controls that prevent runaway costs or unintended side effects.
* Experience evaluating AI tooling for organizational fit: model capability benchmarking, security and data residency posture, SSO/SCIM integration requirements, rate limit and cost modeling at scale, and shadow IT risk when teams self\\-adopt without guardrails.

**Life at Lennar**

At Lennar, we are committed to fostering a supportive and enriching environment for our Associates, offering a comprehensive array of benefits designed to enhance their well\\-being and professional growth. Our Associates have access to robust health insurance plans, including Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage, ensuring their health needs are well taken care of. Our 401(k) Retirement Plan, complete with a $1 for $1 Company Match up to 5%, helps secure their financial future, while Paid Parental Leave and an Associate Assistance Plan provide essential support during life's critical moments. To further support our Associates, we provide an Education Assistance Program and up to $30,000 in Adoption Assistance, underscoring our commitment to their diverse needs and aspirations. From the moment of hire, they can enjoy up to three weeks of vacation annually, alongside generous Holiday, Sick Leave, and Personal Day policies. Additionally, we offer a New Hire Referral Bonus Program, significant Home Purchase Discounts, and unique opportunities such as the Everyone’s Included Day. At Lennar, we believe in investing in our Associates, empowering them to thrive both personally and professionally. Lennar Associates will have access to these benefits as outlined by Lennar’s policies and applicable plan terms. Visit Lennartotalrewards.com to view our suite of benefits.


Join the fun and follow us on social media to see what's happening at our company, and don't forget to connect with us on Lennar: Overview \\| LinkedIn\\< https://www.linkedin.com/company/lennar/ \\> for the latest job opportunities.

Our job is to help you succeed.

  


**About the Client:**

  



We're hiring a technically sharp, fast\\-moving Support Engineer to join a two\\-person engineering team at a growing SaaS platform in the nonprofit fundraising space. This is a hybrid support\\-and\\-development role — you'll own the morning support queue, resolve bugs independently, and progressively take on deeper technical work as you build codebase familiarity.



You'll be working directly alongside the technical co\\-founder. There is no senior engineer to escalate to, no large team to absorb tickets, and no hand\\-holding during onboarding. This role is for someone who thrives in exactly that environment.

  


**Responsibilities:**

  


* Own the L1 support queue (9am–1pm): triage, respond to, and resolve customer\\-facing technical issues independently
* Handle L2 bug resolution: root cause analysis, fixes, and escalation judgment across the application and database layers
* Navigate and debug an existing proprietary codebase you didn't write — quickly and without extensive guidance
* Shift into feature development and deeper technical work in the afternoons as ramp\\-up progresses
* Communicate ticket status and blockers proactively — without waiting to be asked
* Work within a Microsoft stack: C\\#, ASP.NET MVC, SQL Server, Azure

  


**Who This Role Is For:**

  



You're a "figure it out" operator. When handed an unfamiliar system with a bug and no documentation, your instinct is to dig in — not to wait for someone to walk you through it. **You'll resolve 3–5\\+ bugs per day, not one or two. You think in 30\\-minute sprints, not multi\\-hour deep dives.** Speed is the filter for this role — not just the ability to solve problems, but the ability to solve them fast and move on.



Specifically, you:


* Target 3\\+ resolved tickets daily during normal periods, scaling to 5\\+ during demand spikes — carry\\-over is the exception, not the habit
* Have debugged codebases you didn't build — and are comfortable doing so under time pressure
* Know when to escalate and when to keep going (and won't confuse the two)
* Can context\\-switch between a customer\\-facing L1 ticket and a technical L2 bug in the same morning
* Are energized by problem variety, not deep specialization in a single domain


**Requirements**


* 3–5 years of software development experience (full\\-stack or backend\\-leaning)
* Hands\\-on experience with the Microsoft stack: C\\#, ASP.NET MVC, SQL Server
* Demonstrated ability to debug unfamiliar codebases independently
* Front\\-end basics: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery, Bootstrap
* Strong written English — clear, direct, proactive communicator
* Comfortable working in a lean startup environment with minimal documentation and real ownership


**A Note on the Codebase**



The platform is proprietary and built primarily by the co\\-founder. This isn't a well\\-documented, multi\\-team system with established conventions — it's one person's architecture, and you'll be learning its logic rather than refactoring it. That's not a problem for the right candidate; it's actually the interesting part. But if you rely on structured onboarding and thorough documentation to get up to speed, this environment will be a friction point.


**Bonus Points**


* Background in support engineering, developer support, or a hybrid dev/support role
* Experience with Azure infrastructure
* Prior work at a startup or on a very small engineering team
* **Comfortable with AI\\-assisted development — the team actively uses Claude for architectural work and expects you to be a co\\-user, not a skeptic.** If you've integrated AI tooling into your daily workflow, say so.


**Environment \\& Onboarding**



This is a remote\\-first role. You'll start on L1 support during a slower season (June–August), which serves as your product immersion period before L2 responsibilities increase. The team is small, the culture is direct and warm, and the client invests genuinely in the people they bring on — but expects to feel that investment paying off early.

  


**Compensation \\& Benefits (to be provided by Offshore Launch):**


* Up to $3100/mo depending on experience
* Annual bonus up to 150% of one month's salary, contingent on quarterly performance scores
* 13th month pay
* Performance\\-based bonuses
* Comprehensive HMO policy, including dependents.
* Annual continuing education budget to support professional development

  


**Note:**



The Client is not involved in compensation or benefits. As an employee of Offshore Launch, all compensation and benefits are to be provided by the Agency.
